samples.summary: New image-src gate rejects backend-relative `/images/<id>` sources — the canonical form this repo's own docs image uploader produces — so every existing consumer of `serializeMarkdown` (CLI `docs content --format md`, and the new frontend Markdown export) silently degrades those images to `[image]`.
samples.evidence: `isSafeImageSrc` accepts only a `data:image/...;base64` payload or an `isSafeUrl` (absolute, safe-protocol) URL; `packages/core/src/url/index.ts:24` rejects anything without a scheme (`packages/core/test/url.test.ts:20` pins `example.com` → false). But docs image sources are routinely relative: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:12-18` (`resolveImageUrl`) returns the raw `/images/<id>` path unchanged when `VITE_BACKEND_API_URL` is empty, and that value is what `docsImageUploader` (export-utils.ts:39) writes into the model. `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-image-painter.ts:58-63` explicitly documents `/images/abc` as a real src form the editor stores. Those images previously serialized as `![alt](/images/abc)` and now become the `[image]` placeholder with no signal. Fix belongs on the new gate (allow scheme-less relative paths, or resolve them before serializing).

samples.summary: The same gate silently drops relative / fragment hyperlinks (`#bookmark`, `/doc/x`) from Markdown output for all pre-existing callers, not just unsafe schemes.
samples.evidence: `isSafeUrl` returns false for any scheme-less href (packages/core/test/url.test.ts:19-21), and the diff's own test asserts `'/not/absolute'` now serializes as bare text. Hrefs typed through `normalizeLinkUrl` are always absolute, but hrefs arriving from DOCX/HTML import or a CRDT written by another client are not validated on the way in (the diff's comment says so), so an internal or anchor link exported via `packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129` or the new `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/text-actions.ts:44` loses its target with no warning. Fix belongs on the new gate if relative links are meant to survive.

samples.summary: The body-context toolbar now hard-requires two brand-new `EditorAPI` members (`hasCopiedFormat`, `onCopiedFormatChange`) on every editor object handed to it; any partial stub or adapter passed in body context throws instead of degrading.
samples.evidence: `FormatPainterToggle` calls `editor.hasCopiedFormat()` and `editor.onCopiedFormatChange(...)` in its effect with only a `!editor` null-check (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:104-110 in the new code). Existing partial stubs survive only because they mount the header/footer slim toolbar, which returns at docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:539 before this component: packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts:138 and packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar-header-footer.test.tsx:39. Any future or non-test body-context caller with a `as unknown as EditorAPI` cast (the repo's prevailing stub idiom, and unchecked since frontend has no tsc) will crash on mount; optional-calling the two reads would make the toggle degrade instead.

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo: markdown.ts:246-252 gates image srcs to a data:image base64 payload or isSafeUrl, and core/src/url/index.ts:24-31 returns false for any scheme-less URL (its own doc comment at :21-23 states this), so `/images/<id>` falls through to the `[image]` placeholder at markdown.ts:267-270. Relative `/images/<id>` is a genuine stored src form here: frontend export-utils.ts:12-18 returns the raw path when VITE_BACKEND_API_URL is empty and docsImageUploader (export-utils.ts:39) persists exactly that; the CLI maintains a mirrored resolver for scheme-less srcs (cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:48-63, pinned by cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts:44,62); pdf-image-painter.ts:58-63 names `/images/abc` as a real editor-stored form. Both out-of-diff consumers pass the unresolved document: cli/src/docs/content.ts:129 and frontend/src/app/docs/text-actions.ts:44 (the latter explicitly delegating URL safety to the serializer at :36-38). No guard or pre-resolution step makes this unreachable, and no test in docs/test/serialize/markdown.test.ts covers a relative image src. In lane for blast-radius (behaviour change to an exported symbol silently degrading other consumers) and major under the rubric.
